problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=x+2y,\,y(0)=\frac{1}{4}
$$

Use the trapezoidal method with one step to approximate $y\,(\frac{1}{2}),$ rounded to two decimal places.

$$
y\,(\frac{1}{2})≈{{field-1}}
$$
worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

First, since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=\frac{1}{2},$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=\frac{1}{2}-0=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(x+2y+({x}_{\text{new}}+2{y}_{\text{new}}))\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(x+2y+{x}_{\text{new}}+2{y}_{\text{new}}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(x+2y+{x}_{\text{new}})+\frac{1}{2}{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{1}{4}(x+2y+{x}_{\text{new}})+\frac{1}{2}{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{4}(x+{x}_{\text{new}}+6y)+\frac{1}{2}{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{4}(x+{x}_{\text{new}}+6y) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{2}(x+{x}_{\text{new}}+6y)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is ${x}_{\text{new}}=0+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}.$
 Hence, the new $y$ value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{2}(x+{x}_{\text{new}}+6y) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(0+\frac{1}{2}+6\cdot \frac{1}{4}) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y\,(\frac{1}{2})≈1.00.$
